why: platform.definer_client_grant_grandfather rows whose function has no platform.client_callable_door row. This is the 2026-08-28 snapshot (db-rules FEATURE.md §6d-4): every SECURITY DEFINER function alive that day was grandfathered so day one stripped zero live doors, and almost none of them was ever declared a door. A grandfather row means the §6d-4 event trigger STANDS DOWN for that function, so each of these is a place where a future default or hand-written GRANT re-opens a client door silently. That is exactly how DD-098 happened. This number may only SHRINK - never raise it to clear a finding. Shrink it by declaring the door (platform.client_callable_door) when the function really is client-callable, or by deleting the grandfather row when it is not. Lower this file to match whenever the count drops.
